title: Demeter and Persephone
text:
Persephone, daughter of Demeter the goddess of grain, was picking flowers in a meadow with her friends when she reached for a wonderful narcissus. At that moment the earth split open, and Hades, lord of the dead, rose in a golden chariot and carried her off to the underworld. Zeus, her father, had agreed to it without telling her mother.

Demeter heard her daughter's cry and searched the earth for nine days, carrying torches and refusing to eat or bathe. When she learned the truth from the Sun, she abandoned Olympus in anger. Disguised as an old woman, she went to Eleusis, where she served as nursemaid in a royal household.

Then she made the earth barren. Seed would not sprout and the fields produced nothing. People began to starve, and the gods received no offerings. Zeus sent one god after another to persuade her, but she refused to let anything grow until she saw her daughter again.

At last Zeus sent Hermes to bring Persephone back. Before she left, Hades gave her a pomegranate seed to eat. Mother and daughter were reunited with great joy. But because she had eaten food of the dead, Persephone had to return below for a third of every year. When she comes up again, the fields grow green and the earth flowers.
lesson: When a family must share a child between two homes, the arrangement may be painful but can still let everyone live. Grief and reunion can take turns.
